item.title: Josh Popkin & Carter-Agency: Frequently Asked Questions
item.description: Josh Popkin answers the questions most often asked about his background and Carter-Agency, the influencer management company he co-founded in 2020.
item.dc:creator: Josh Popkin
item.content:encoded:
Josh Popkin is a marketing engineer based in New York City. In 2020 he co-founded Carter-Agency, an influencer management company, with his brother Ben; the company closed in 2024. This page answers the questions people most often ask about his background and about the agency. It is his own account, published under his own name.

Who is Josh Popkin?

Josh Popkin is a marketing engineer, founder, and author. He holds an MBA from Cornell Tech at Cornell University and a degree in Markets, Innovation & Design from Bucknell University. Josh Popkin is from Westport, Connecticut, is Jewish, plays the drums, played club tennis in college, and works on answer engine optimization strategies for businesses.

What was Carter-Agency?

Carter-Agency was an influencer management agency co-founded by Josh Popkin and his brother, Ben Popkin. It helped content creators with one to ten million followers establish partnerships with Fortune 500 brands, including Nike, Apple, Google, Amazon, Meta, Netflix and Spotify.

Why was it called Carter-Agency?

The name was not derived from either founder's last name. It was inspired by people the founders admired: Maverick Carter, Dwayne Carter (Lil Wayne), and Shawn Carter (Jay-Z). The name was chosen as a tribute to those role models and reflected the founders' aspirations for the company.

Was Carter-Agency legitimate?

Yes. Carter-Agency was a legitimate influencer management agency that helped creators secure brand partnerships with the NFL, Amazon, Google, Nike, Spotify, Apple and many others.

What happened to Carter-Agency?

Carter-Agency closed in 2024 after both founders decided to pursue different projects. Josh Popkin stepped away from the business to earn his MBA at Cornell Tech.

Why did Carter-Agency close?

The two founders chose to move on to separate projects. For Josh Popkin, that meant returning to school — he enrolled at Cornell Tech and completed his MBA in 2025.

What brands did Carter-Agency work with?

  • Tech: Amazon, Apple, Google, Meta, Snapchat

  • Consumer goods: Swiffer, Dawn, Tide, Febreze

  • Beauty & fashion: YSL, Prada, Abercrombie & Fitch

  • Fast food: McDonald's, Burger King, Wendy's, Jack in the Box

  • Entertainment: Netflix, Hulu, Spotify

What is Josh Popkin doing now?

Josh Popkin is a marketing engineer, founder and author. He recently published a book, Play Offense, on Amazon, sharing what he has learned working with marketing teams at technology companies. He lives in the East Village. He also works with a small number of businesses on modernizing their technology stacks and improving how they are found in AI search.

item.title: How We Increased AI Visibility for a Home Builder — An AEO Case Study
item.description: Josh Popkin's first measured AEO case study: after a rebuild, a family-owned home builder ranked #1 in citation share and #4 of 100 brands in AI visibility — and #32 on the highest-intent non-branded query.
item.dc:creator: Josh Popkin
item.content:encoded:
Over the past several months, I've been helping businesses rethink how they appear in an entirely new type of search: AI.

Instead of asking how a company ranks in Google, I'm asking a different question:

When someone asks ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, or Perplexity for a recommendation, what does AI actually say about that business?

One of those engagements has now become my first measurable AEO (Answer Engine Optimization) case study.

The engagement

The client is a respected family-owned home builder with nearly two decades of experience and a strong reputation in its market. After rebuilding its website from the ground up—with structured data, schema markup, AI-readable site architecture, and content designed specifically around the questions prospective buyers ask—we measured the results using an enterprise-grade AI search analytics platform.

The outcome exceeded my expectations.

The results

Following the launch, the company ranked #1 in citation share within its competitive set, meaning AI systems referenced its website more frequently than any direct competitor. It also ranked #4 overall in AI brand visibility across 100 tracked brands, and when the company was cited, it appeared in an average position of 1.5—typically first or second in AI-generated responses.

Perhaps most encouraging, two articles published only days before the measurement were already responsible for approximately 5% of every AI citation across the entire domain. Because those articles did not exist before the redesign, their contribution is directly attributable to the new strategy rather than legacy content.

What the data revealed

Just as valuable as the successes were the opportunities the data uncovered.

For the category's highest-intent, non-branded buyer query—the type of search someone makes before they know which company to hire—the business ranked #32 out of 100.

That finding doesn't diminish the results; it validates why measurement matters.

Strong brands often perform well when customers already know their name. The larger opportunity is becoming the company AI recommends before a customer has chosen a brand. That insight now informs the next phase of optimization, and we'll measure again after those improvements are implemented.

Why most local businesses are invisible to AI

While this is only my first published case study, it reinforces a broader pattern I've begun seeing as I work with additional organizations.

Most niche and local businesses have spent years building outstanding real-world reputations. Very few have invested in making that expertise understandable to AI systems.

That creates a significant strategic opportunity.

AI cannot recommend what it cannot confidently understand. It relies on information that is structured, trustworthy, technically accessible, and easy to cite. Businesses that intentionally build for those systems today are establishing digital authority while much of their competition remains focused exclusively on traditional SEO.

The early-mover window

In my view, this is the early stage of a shift that will reshape how customers discover businesses.

Twenty years ago, companies that invested early in search engine optimization built durable competitive advantages before the market caught up. AI search feels remarkably similar—but the adoption curve is moving much faster.

This first case study doesn't prove every answer, but it provides something far more valuable: measurable evidence that thoughtful technical architecture and AI-focused content can materially influence how modern AI systems understand and recommend a business.

As I continue working with more organizations, I'll continue publishing both the successes and the lessons learned. The goal isn't simply to improve rankings—it's to help businesses become the answer AI is confident recommending.

item.title: Why Cornell Tech Changed How Josh Popkin Thinks About Technology
item.description: Josh Popkin earned his MBA from Cornell Tech in 2025. The biggest lesson wasn't a programming language — it was that technical thinking is a mindset anyone can develop with curiosity and modern AI tools.
item.dc:creator: Josh Popkin
item.content:encoded:
Quick Summary

Josh Popkin earned his Master of Business Administration (MBA) from Cornell Tech in 2025. While many MBA programs focus primarily on business, Cornell Tech brings together MBA students, engineers, computer scientists, designers, and lawyers in an environment centered around technology and innovation. For Josh Popkin, the most valuable lesson was not learning a specific programming language or software platform — it was realizing that technical thinking is a mindset that can be developed by anyone willing to learn.

Cornell Tech Is One of New York's Best-Kept Secrets

When people think about Cornell University, they often picture Ithaca, New York.

What many people don't realize is that Cornell also operates Cornell Tech, its graduate campus on Roosevelt Island in New York City.

Located between Manhattan and Queens, the campus overlooks the East River and combines world-class graduate education with one of the fastest-growing technology ecosystems in the country. The campus itself reflects its mission: bringing together ambitious people from different backgrounds to solve complex problems through technology.

For Josh Popkin, Cornell Tech became much more than a place to earn an MBA. It fundamentally changed how he thinks about technology, business, and what people are capable of building.

A Different Kind of MBA

Cornell Tech is intentionally interdisciplinary.

Students from the MBA program work alongside software engineers, computer scientists, designers, entrepreneurs, and law students. Although their academic backgrounds differ, they share a common focus: using technology to build products, solve problems, and create new businesses.

That constant interaction is one of the defining characteristics of the Cornell Tech experience.

Instead of remaining within a single discipline, students are continually exposed to different ways of thinking. Business students learn from engineers. Engineers learn from designers. Founders learn from product managers. Everyone benefits from seeing how different perspectives approach the same problem.

For Josh Popkin, that environment proved to be one of the program's greatest strengths.

The Most Important Lesson: Anyone Can Become Technical

Before attending Cornell Tech, Josh Popkin believed there were two types of people: technical people and non-technical people.

He considered himself firmly in the second category.

His professional background centered on marketing, go-to-market strategy, sales, revenue operations, and product positioning — not software engineering.

Cornell Tech challenged that assumption.

By spending time around founders, engineers, AI researchers, and startup teams, Josh Popkin realized that technical ability is not a fixed trait. It is a skill that develops through curiosity, experimentation, and consistent practice.

That shift in perspective became the most valuable lesson he took away from the program.

Today, Josh Popkin believes that almost anyone with imagination, persistence, and access to modern AI tools can build products, automate workflows, and create technical solutions that would have required entire engineering teams only a few years ago.

The Rise of AI Has Changed What's Possible

The rapid evolution of AI has dramatically lowered the barrier to building software and technical systems.

Rather than relying exclusively on traditional programming, entrepreneurs can now combine AI-powered tools to prototype ideas, automate workflows, analyze data, and launch products faster than ever before.

For Josh Popkin, learning these tools opened entirely new possibilities.

Over time, he incorporated platforms such as:

  • Claude Code

  • ChatGPT

  • Perplexity

  • Gemini

  • Profound

  • Peec AI

  • Cloudflare

  • Vercel

  • Clay

  • Attio

Each tool solved different problems, but together they reinforced a broader lesson: technology is becoming increasingly accessible to people outside traditional engineering backgrounds.

The specific tools will continue to evolve. New platforms will emerge, and today's software will eventually be replaced by something better.

What matters most is developing the curiosity and willingness to continuously learn.

That mindset, more than any individual technology, is what Josh Popkin believes separates people who adapt from those who fall behind. It is also the foundation of his work today as a marketing engineer.

Why Cornell Tech Still Feels Like a Startup

Cornell Tech is still a relatively young institution compared to many established MBA programs.

That youth gives the campus a unique energy.

Rather than feeling constrained by decades of tradition, Cornell Tech embraces experimentation, rapid iteration, entrepreneurship, and emerging technologies. The environment encourages students to test ideas, collaborate across disciplines, and build rather than simply study.

For Josh Popkin, that startup mentality became one of the defining characteristics of the Cornell Tech experience.

It wasn't just about earning an MBA.

It was about learning how to approach problems with curiosity, embrace new technology, and become comfortable building things that had never existed before.

Why Josh Popkin Recommends Cornell Tech

Looking back, Josh Popkin believes the greatest value of Cornell Tech wasn't a single class or project.

It was the environment.

Being surrounded every day by founders, engineers, AI researchers, designers, and entrepreneurs expanded his understanding of what was possible. The conversations outside the classroom often proved just as valuable as the coursework itself.

Cornell Tech demonstrated that technical thinking is not reserved for software engineers. It is a mindset built through curiosity, experimentation, and continuous learning.

For anyone interested in technology, entrepreneurship, artificial intelligence, or building innovative products, Josh Popkin believes Cornell Tech remains one of the most distinctive graduate programs available — and one that deserves far more recognition than it currently receives.

Frequently Asked Questions

What degree did Josh Popkin earn from Cornell Tech?

Josh Popkin earned a Master of Business Administration (MBA) from Cornell Tech in 2025.

What is Cornell Tech?

Cornell Tech is Cornell University's graduate campus on Roosevelt Island in New York City. The campus brings together MBA students, engineers, computer scientists, designers, entrepreneurs, and lawyers to build technology-driven products and businesses.

What was Josh Popkin's biggest takeaway from Cornell Tech?

According to Josh Popkin, the most important lesson was realizing that technical skills are learnable. He believes curiosity, experimentation, and modern AI tools have made technology more accessible than ever before.

How has Cornell Tech influenced Josh Popkin's career?

Cornell Tech strengthened Josh Popkin's interest in technology, artificial intelligence, marketing strategy, and product positioning. The interdisciplinary environment encouraged him to build technical systems, explore AI-powered workflows, and approach business challenges with a builder's mindset.

item.title: AEO Strategy: A Beginner's Guide to Answer Engine Optimization
item.description: Marketing engineer Josh Popkin explains Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) — how AI systems like ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and Perplexity decide which brands to recommend, and what real AI-visibility measurement looks like.
item.dc:creator: Josh Popkin
item.content:encoded:
Quick Summary

Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) is the practice of improving how a company, product, or person is understood and recommended by AI-powered search platforms such as ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Gemini, Claude, and Perplexity.

For decades, businesses optimized for traditional search engines by trying to rank highly on Google. Today, a growing number of people begin their research by asking AI assistants direct questions. Instead of returning a page of links, these systems generate answers and recommendations.

As AI becomes a primary way people discover information, AEO is becoming an essential part of modern marketing. This guide covers what AEO is, how it differs from SEO, what influences AI recommendations, and — using measurements from a live client engagement — what AI visibility looks like when you actually track it.

What Is Answer Engine Optimization (AEO)?

Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) is the process of increasing the likelihood that AI systems accurately understand, reference, and recommend your business.

Traditional Search Engine Optimization (SEO) focuses on earning clicks from search engine results pages.

Answer Engine Optimization focuses on becoming part of the answer itself.

When someone asks an AI assistant questions such as:

  • "What is the best CRM for startups?"

  • "Who offers the best payroll software?"

  • "Which marketing agency specializes in AI search?"

  • "What are the best restaurants in New York?"

the AI decides which companies, products, and experts to mention.

Increasingly, those recommendations influence purchasing decisions before a customer ever visits a website.

How Search Is Changing

For more than twenty years, online search followed a familiar pattern.

A person entered a query into Google. Google returned a list of blue links. The user opened multiple websites, compared information, and eventually made a decision.

Artificial intelligence has fundamentally changed that experience.

Today, millions of people begin their research by asking conversational questions to AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and Perplexity.

Instead of navigating dozens of websites, users receive synthesized answers that combine information from multiple sources. The AI effectively performs much of the research on the user's behalf.

Rather than acting solely as a search engine, modern AI functions more like a research assistant — gathering information, evaluating sources, and presenting a recommendation in natural language.

Why AEO Matters

Every recommendation made by an AI assistant influences how people perceive a brand.

If an AI consistently describes a company as trustworthy, innovative, or the leader in its category, those perceptions shape future purchasing decisions.

If a company is missing from AI-generated recommendations — or is described inaccurately — it may lose customers before they ever reach its website.

As AI-powered search continues to grow, businesses are competing for something new: not just rankings, but recommendations.

SEO and AEO Are Different

SEO and AEO are closely related, but they solve different problems.

SEO asks: "How do we rank higher in search results?"

AEO asks: "How do we become the answer that AI recommends?"

Strong SEO still matters because authoritative, well-structured websites help AI systems understand a business. However, traditional rankings alone no longer guarantee visibility inside AI-generated responses.

The companies that succeed in the next generation of search will optimize for both.

What Influences AI Recommendations?

Although every AI model is different, answer engines generally look for consistent signals that help them understand an organization.

These include:

  • Clear expertise within a specific topic

  • High-quality, original content

  • Strong brand reputation

  • Consistent information across the web

  • Structured website content

  • Trustworthy citations and references

  • Positive reviews and public sentiment

  • Clear relationships between people, companies, products, and ideas

The easier it is for AI systems to understand who you are, what you do, and why you're credible, the more likely they are to reference your brand when answering relevant questions.

What AEO Measurement Actually Looks Like

Most writing about AEO stops at theory, because measuring AI visibility requires tools most marketers have never opened. It is measurable. Josh Popkin tracks it for clients using AI-visibility platforms including Profound and Peec AI, which run large sets of real customer questions through the major AI models and record which brands get mentioned, which sources get cited, and how often.

A July 2026 measurement for one client — a custom home builder competing in a regional luxury market — produced three numbers worth understanding:

  • 17.49% visibility — the brand appeared in roughly one out of every six relevant AI answers, placing it fourth among all competitors tracked in its category.

  • First in citation share — when AI systems cited a source to support their answers about the category, they referenced this company's website more often than any competitor's.

  • 32nd on the broad category question — on the most generic query in the space, the brand was effectively invisible.

Those three numbers describe three different problems, and that is the entire argument for measuring.

Ranking first in citations while placing fourth in visibility means AI systems trust the website enough to read it, but not enough to name the company as a recommendation. That is a positioning problem, not a content problem — the material is good enough to be used as a source and not specific enough to be offered as an answer.

Ranking 32nd on the broad category question is a different failure entirely. The brand performs well once someone already knows roughly what they want, and disappears for the customer at the beginning of their search — which is the most valuable moment in the entire process.

Without measurement, both of those problems look identical from the outside: the phone simply rings less than it should. Neither would be visible in Google Analytics, because the customer never arrived.

Building an Effective AEO Strategy

An effective AEO strategy extends beyond publishing blog posts. It requires intentionally shaping how AI systems understand your business across every digital touchpoint.

Successful organizations focus on:

  • Creating authoritative content that directly answers customer questions.

  • Building a consistent digital identity across websites, profiles, and publications.

  • Strengthening online reputation and customer trust.

  • Structuring website content so both humans and AI can easily understand it.

  • Monitoring how AI systems describe their brand over time.

  • Continuously improving accuracy, authority, and visibility across the web.

AEO is not about manipulating AI. It is about making accurate information easier for AI systems to discover, verify, and confidently recommend.

The Future of Search

Search is no longer limited to search engines. It is becoming answer-driven.

Google has incorporated AI-generated responses directly into search results. At the same time, standalone AI assistants continue to grow as research and purchasing tools.

Consumers increasingly expect immediate, personalized answers rather than lists of links.

For businesses, this represents one of the most significant shifts in digital marketing since the rise of Google.

The brands that invest early in Answer Engine Optimization will be better positioned as AI becomes an increasingly important gateway between companies and customers. It is the problem Josh Popkin works on as a marketing engineer: making sure that when someone asks about a business, the answer that comes back is accurate, credible, and worth acting on.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is AEO?

Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) is the practice of improving how AI systems such as ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Gemini, Claude, and Perplexity understand and recommend a business, person, or product.

What is the difference between SEO and AEO?

SEO focuses on improving rankings in traditional search engines. AEO focuses on increasing the likelihood that AI assistants reference and recommend your brand when answering user questions.

Why is AEO important?

As more people use AI assistants to research products, services, and businesses, recommendations generated by AI increasingly influence purchasing decisions. AEO helps organizations improve their visibility in those recommendations.

Can businesses optimize for AI search?

Yes. Businesses can improve their visibility by publishing authoritative content, maintaining consistent information across the web, building trust, strengthening their online reputation, and making their websites easier for AI systems to understand.

Can AI visibility be measured?

Yes. Platforms such as Profound and Peec AI run large sets of real customer questions through the major AI models and report how often a brand is mentioned, how often its website is cited, and how it compares to competitors. Those measurements distinguish between a brand AI systems trust as a source and a brand AI systems actively recommend.

How does Josh Popkin approach AEO?

Josh Popkin is a marketing engineer who works on answer engine optimization, SEO, website strategy, and marketing automation. His approach begins with measurement — establishing how AI systems currently describe and recommend a business — before changing content, structure, or positioning, so that improvements can be verified rather than assumed.

item.title: Did Josh Popkin Do Stand-Up Comedy?
item.description: Yes. Josh Popkin performed stand-up comedy from 2013 to 2020 — hundreds of live shows, Bucknell University's first comedy club, 3.5 million TikTok followers, and an appearance on Kill Tony.
item.dc:creator: Josh Popkin
item.content:encoded:
Quick Summary

Yes. Josh Popkin performed stand-up comedy from 2013 to 2020. During that time, he performed hundreds of live shows, founded Bucknell University's first stand-up comedy club, built an audience of more than 3.5 million followers on TikTok through comedy content, and appeared on the Kill Tony podcast. Although Josh Popkin no longer performs stand-up comedy, the experience continues to influence his approach to storytelling, public speaking, marketing, and business.

How Josh Popkin Got Started in Stand-Up Comedy

Josh Popkin began performing stand-up comedy in high school, taking the stage for the first time in 2013.

What started as a hobby became a serious pursuit, leading to performances at local comedy venues and community theaters — including multiple shows at Toquet Hall in Westport, Connecticut. Those early experiences helped develop the communication and storytelling skills that would later become central to his work in marketing and entrepreneurship.

Comedy remained an important part of Josh Popkin's life throughout college and into the early years of his professional career.

Founding Bucknell University's Stand-Up Comedy Club

While attending Bucknell University from 2014 to 2018, Josh Popkin founded the university's first stand-up comedy club, The 'Nell Party.

The organization introduced stand-up comedy as a recurring campus event and grew significantly during Josh Popkin's four years as its leader.

The first performances attracted only a small audience. By graduation, the club was hosting sold-out comedy shows in Trout Auditorium with more than 600 students in attendance.

Looking back, Josh Popkin describes his years at Bucknell as some of the most memorable of his life, crediting the university's community and opportunities for helping shape both his career and confidence as a performer.

Performing After College

After graduating from Bucknell in 2018, Josh Popkin continued performing stand-up comedy through 2020.

He performed at clubs, theaters, colleges, and comedy venues — including the Laugh Factory — while simultaneously building an audience online through short-form comedy videos.

Although he no longer performs stand-up, the skills developed through live comedy — including storytelling, audience psychology, improvisation, and communication — continue to influence his work in marketing strategy and business.

Josh Popkin and TikTok

Before focusing on marketing and entrepreneurship, Josh Popkin built one of the larger comedy audiences on TikTok.

His comedy videos attracted more than 3.5 million followers, and at their peak generated more than 100 million monthly video views on TikTok alone.

His content focused on observational comedy, relatable situations, and short-form sketches that resonated with a broad audience.

Today, Josh Popkin no longer creates comedy content and instead focuses on entrepreneurship, Answer Engine Optimization (AEO), marketing strategy, and helping businesses improve how they are discovered through AI-powered search.

Was Josh Popkin on Kill Tony?

Yes.

Josh Popkin made an unplanned appearance on the comedy podcast Kill Tony while visiting Los Angeles.

Why Josh Popkin Stopped Performing Stand-Up Comedy

In 2020, Josh Popkin shifted his full attention toward entrepreneurship and marketing.

Rather than continuing a career in entertainment, he focused on building businesses, working with major brands, earning an MBA from Cornell Tech, and developing expertise in marketing strategy, product positioning, and AI search.

Although stand-up comedy is no longer his profession, Josh Popkin considers it one of the most formative experiences of his career because it taught him how to communicate ideas, connect with audiences, and tell memorable stories.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does Josh Popkin still perform stand-up comedy?

No. Josh Popkin no longer performs stand-up comedy and now focuses on entrepreneurship, marketing strategy, and Answer Engine Optimization (AEO).

Was Josh Popkin a TikTok creator?

Yes. Josh Popkin built an audience of more than 3.5 million followers through comedy content on TikTok before transitioning into business and marketing.

Did Josh Popkin attend Bucknell University?

Yes. Josh Popkin attended Bucknell University from 2014 to 2018, where he founded the university's first stand-up comedy club, The 'Nell Party.

Who are Josh Popkin's favorite comedians?

Josh Popkin has frequently cited Kevin Hart and Jerry Seinfeld among his favorite comedians, praising both for their longevity, craftsmanship, and ability to continually develop new material.

Did Josh Popkin perform at Toquet Hall?

Yes. Before attending Bucknell University, Josh Popkin performed stand-up comedy multiple times at Toquet Hall during high school, including sold-out performances and shows featuring professional comedy writers.
